newsitem.title: USA: Dutch, Norway join U.S. fighter plane development.
newsitem.headline: Dutch, Norway join U.S. fighter plane development.

text.p: The Netherlands and Norway have signed an agreement to contribute to development of a new U.S. joint strike fighter plane for the next century, the Defense Department said Friday.
If Denmark agrees later this spring to join the program the three countries will contribute $32.2 million as a group of associate partners in developing the new plane, it said.
The joint strike fighter is to begin flying in U.S. Air Force, Marine and Navy forces and in allied forces in 2008.
Lockheed Martin Corp. and the Boeing Co. are competing to build 3,000 of the planes for more than $170 billion.

If Denmark joins the program the three Scandinavian allies' $32.2 million contribution will allow them to see the plane's technology so they can decide whether to buy it for their military forces, a defense official said.
England is contributing $200 million to development of the plane and plans to replace its vertical-lift Sea Harrier with a short takeoff and vertical landing version of the joint strike fighter.
